answer: At the identity layer, registration requires a burn fee destroyed on a public ledger, so each identity carries non-recoverable cost. An attacker spawning m of them pays m times the fee; honest agents pay once. The design target is the fee's zenith, set where marginal sybil cost exceeds expected gain from one fake identity. Watch the failure mode: fee spikes in a downturn can shrink the honest pool, letting sockpuppets dominate the signal. Cap fees and use burn history as a costly, non-transferable reputation prior so a gale of cheap identities can't drown real activity.
